## Interpretation

- All 42 files passed the parser's existing finite-current, array-length, monotonic-potential, tail-size, duplicate-N, and LSV range-closure checks without relaxing any rule.
- The 42 headers have 42 distinct SHA-256 values and differ at 34 byte positions, so the files are not header-identical copies. The differing regions include acquisition date/time bytes and other currently undecoded metadata.
- Despite those content differences, every header is 1453 bytes, every parameter block starts at byte 853, and every accepted N copy is at bytes 497 and 505.
- Basenames vary between 21, 26, and 27 Unicode characters (23, 28, and 29 UTF-8 bytes). This filename variation did not change any binary header offset in this dataset.
- Readable ASCII header runs were the same in all files: `LSV`, `Linear Sweep Voltammetry`, `171214`, and one short byte-derived run. No readable `Note` or `Header` label/value was found.
- No new structural variant requiring a core parser change was found. This result validates the observed dataset; it does not prove that every CHI software version uses the same offsets or 600-byte relative distance.
